title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
prompt:
Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix notation). The expression is a list of tokens `tokens`, where each token is either an integer or one of the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`. Division between two integers should truncate toward zero.

It is guaranteed the expression is always valid and evaluates to an integer that fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: tokens[i] is either an operator (+, -, *, /) or an integer in the range [-200, 200]
hints: Postfix notation means each operator applies to the two operands that immediately precede it — you need access to 'the last two values produced'.
A stack is exactly the right structure: push numbers, and when you hit an operator, pop two operands, combine them, and push the result back.
For division, use int(a / b) or a special-case truncation (not floor division //, which rounds toward negative infinity and would be wrong for negative results).

solution.approach: Scan tokens left to right using a stack. Push every numeric token. On an operator, pop the top two values (the second-popped is the left operand, the first-popped is the right operand, since it was pushed later), apply the operator, and push the result back onto the stack. At the end exactly one value remains: the answer. Truncating division toward zero (rather than Python's floor //) is done explicitly via int() on the true division result.
